subject: Deployment path options & MAP runway — decision needed
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Li <andrew.li@clearsighthealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment path options & MAP runway — decision needed

Andrew — attaching the MAP draft we discussed (CSH-MAP-v1.pdf) and a short SOC2 summary for your security team. High level proposal summarized below so legal/procurement and your eng leads have a single view.

Summary (proposal):
- US production: Redwood Hosted (fastest time-to-value).
- EU production (PHI/residency): Dedicated EU cluster (reserved capacity) with EU data egress controls.
- High-risk PHI pilot: Private (on-prem or VPC) for the 1–2 endpoints that need full control — run as a staged pilot after the Dedicated cutover.

Why this split?
- Hosted covers low-risk traffic and lets you ship quickly (2–3 weeks onboarding).
- Dedicated for EU covers residency/SLA/regulatory constraints with predictable capacity and logging audit trails (estimated 4–6 week onboarding).
- Private pilot keeps the most sensitive workflows behind your network controls; longer lead time but smallest blast radius.

Proposed MAP milestones (rough):
1) Decision on mode split (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — target: 2027-04-20
2) Kickoff & Dedicated EU provisioning — target start: 2027-04-25
3) Staged validation & canary traffic — 2027-05-16 to 2027-05-30
4) Private pilot scoping & SOW finalization — target SOW signed: 2027-05-12

Open asks for your team:
- Confirm decision window (can you commit to Apr 20?)
- Any constraints from procurement on contracting cadence or PO timing?
- Security: is SOC2 summary sufficient to start dedicated provisioning or do you need full report upfront?

Attachments: CSH-MAP-v1.pdf (MAP), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — quick responses from our side: great to see the options laid out. A few clarifying Qs before we lock the MAP: 

1) For Dedicated EU — what SLA and uptime guarantees do you offer for reserved pools? Also need an estimated onboarding lead time (calendar weeks) for a mid-sized model workload (6k reqs/min peak).
2) Private on-prem pilot — can Redwood support hybrid KV cache across Private and Dedicated, or would that be a full cutover? We want to avoid duplicate inference state if possible.
3) Procurement: we typically need 45 days for contract review and a PO. Is there flexibility on a short-term trial while legal finishes the SOW review?

Also copying contracts@clearsighthealth.com. Can Laura or Ben chime with technical ramp estimates so we can route this internally?

— Andrew
Andrew Li
Head of AI Ops, ClearSight Health

Andrew — quick technical notes to help procurement/eng triage: 

1) Dedicated EU sizing & onboarding:
- For the model footprint you described (medium transformer serving ~6k reqs/min with mixed short/long context), plan for a 4-week provisioning and smoke test period after purchase order + a single day for baseline validation (assuming access to your test dataset).
- SLA: Dedicated pools are eligible for an SLA addendum; typical target is 99.9% region-level availability for reserved pools (we'll surface the exact language in the SOW).

2) Private pilot considerations:
- Private (on-prem) requires network preparation, KMS/HSM integration, and a short agent deploy — estimate 8–12 weeks from kickoff if you choose fully air-gapped.
- Hybrid cache: we can offer a bridge approach where prefix/KV caching is shared via a secure transit (VPC peering + encrypted cache sync), but it adds complexity and a small consistency window. If minimizing duplication is essential, we recommend starting with Dedicated EU and then shifting the high-sensitivity endpoints into Private during the pilot window.

3) Short-term trial flexibility:
- We can run a 30-day sandbox on Hosted (US) for evaluation while SOW is negotiated; limits apply for PHI. That would keep momentum during legal review.

I attached an estimate workbook (eu-dedicated-onboard-estimate.xlsx) with timeline and resource assumptions. Happy to walk through on a 30-minute call.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Andrew / Contracts team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the procurement note. I captured the follow-ups from Laura into an updated MAP path below and a recommended near-term cadence.

Updated MAP decisions + cadence:
- Decision window: please confirm hosting split by 2027-04-20 (we'll mark Dedicated EU as provisioning start on 2027-04-25 if confirmed).
- Trial option: Redwood will provision a 30-day Hosted sandbox (US only, PHI excluded) to keep your engineers validating prompts and latency while SOW reviews proceed.
- Dedicated EU onboarding: 4 weeks provisioning + 1 week validation once PO is received.
- Private pilot: scope and SOW target by 2027-05-12; pilot schedule estimated 8–12 weeks after SOW execution.

Immediate next actions (I will take these):
1) Drop an updated MAP into the shared Drive (link below) with milestone dates and acceptance criteria.
2) Circulate SOW draft (SOW-draft-v0.2.docx) to your contracts team — please let me know who the primary contracts reviewer is so I can tailor counters and track redlines.
3) Schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff with Laura for Apr 14 to walk the onboarding checklist and test data handoff.

Can contracts@clearsighthealth.com confirm whether a 30-day sandbox is acceptable to start while SOW is in review? If procurement needs a different cadence, share the PO timing and we can adjust milestone dates.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
